newsitem.title: USA: Stocks post biggest loss since July on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Stocks post biggest loss since July on profit-taking.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks tumbled to their biggest loss in nearly five months Tuesday as investors locked in profits from November's rally.
Bonds ended little changed for a second consecutive day.
The British pound fell sharply against other major currencies after a top British government official expressed concern about sterling's recent strength.

"A wave of sell programmes hit the market. Big stocks were punished and small caps performed somewhat better. It appears there was profit-taking after a superb month of market action in November," said Alan Ackerman, a market strategist at Fahnestock and Co.

The Dow Jones industrial average lost 79.01 points, or 1.21 percent, to close at 6,442.69 as huge computer-driven sell programmes hit in a frantic last 10 minutes of trading. It was the blue-chip index's biggest one-day point drop since it fell 161.05 points on July 15 amid earnings jitters.
The Dow soared about 500 points, or 8 percent, in November and many were awaiting a pullback.
In the broader market, gainers beat losers 1,294 to 1,192 on very heavy volume of about 516 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

The broader market also ended well off its highs, although the technology-studded Nasdaq Composite managed a small gain that set its seventh consecutive record. The index rose 0.55 to 1,300.37, its first finish above 1,300.
"This is the type of blow-off the market needs to take a little wind out of the sails," said Douglas Myers of Interstate Johnson/Lane. "Give it a chance to rebalance, reallocate and wax philosophic."
Bellwether International Business Machines Corp., which hit a nine-year high earlier in the day of 166, ended down 3/8 at 162-5/8 -- its first lower close in about two weeks.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond fell 2/32, raising its yield to 6.37 percent from 6.36 percent on Monday.

The pound slid against the mark, the yen and the dollar, falling to a one-month low against the U.S. currency before ending the session at $1.6445, over three-and-a-half cents lower than its close Monday at $1.6802.
In other trading, the dollar was mixed, climbing modestly to 1.5565 marks from 1.5555 at Monday's close, but sliding against the yen to 113.27 from 114.53.
Wheat prices tumbled on news that Australia may harvest the second-largest ever crop of 21.3 million metric tons.

Chicago Board of Trade March soft red winter wheat closed down 5-1/4 cents at $3.72 a bushel. The December contract closed 8-1/4 cents lower at $3.85, after 700,000 bushels were posted for delivery against that contract.

New York Mercantile Exchange crude oil futures recovered from early losses to close higher and gasoline posted strong gains for the second consecutive session, both in reaction to a refinery workers' strike in France.
January gasoline rose 1.01 cents to 69.13 cents a gallon and January crude oil added 13 cents at $24.93 a barrel while January heating oil gained 0.65 cent to 74.22.
Overseas, London's FTSE 100 index rose 23.0 points to 4,061.5. In Japan, the key Nikkei 225 average fell 44.13 points to 20,630.56.
